newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Lloyds Bank gets HK banking licence.
newsitem.headline: Lloyds Bank gets HK banking licence.

text.p: The Hong Kong Monetary Authority said on Thursday it had granted a restricted banking licence to Lloyds Bank Plc. Lloyds Bank is a wholly-owned subsidiary of Lloyds TSB Group Plc.

The HKMA, the territory's de facto central bank, said in a statement the reason for Lloyds Bank's application to operate a branch in Hong Kong was to take over the business of its unit, Hill Samuel Bank, as part of its restructuring process.
It said the principle activities of Hill Samuel Bank are the provision of mortgage loans.
After granting the licence to Lloyds Bank, the number of restricted licence banks in Hong Kong has increased to 64.
